analysis.text: Pass-first point guard with excellent floor vision and handle.  Very strong and super athletic.  A tenacious defender.  Great quickness and leaping ability. Excels taking his man to the basket.  Virtually unstoppable one-on-one.  Great size for his position.  Excellent floor leader.
Needs to work on his jump-shot consistency -- especially from distance.  A poor free-throw shooter.

As a senior in 2006-07, averaged 25 points, 9 rebounds, 8 assists, 3.4
Rose's ballhandling skills helped Memphis reach the title game.
(Nick Laham/Getty Images)

steals and 1.0 blocks while shooting 59 percent from the field and 45 percent from 3-point range to help Simeon (Ill.) finish 33-2 and capture its second consecutive Class AA state title.
Top 2

The best pure point guard in the draft draws some comparisons to both Deron Williams and Chris Paul.  He has the strength and defensive presence of Williams and the speed and quickness of Paul.  Looks like a lock for a Top 2 pick and a potential No. 1 pick depending on who gets the No. 2 pick.

It was a foregone conclusion ... and the right pick. Though Beasley is an offensive force, Rose gives the Bulls leadership, athleticism, defense and a winning attitude. He will make everyone in Chicago better and quickly help turn around a franchise in desperate need of a shot in the arm.
Brings leadership and winning attitude.

Great athlete with long arms.  Deep, deep range on his jump shot.  Excellent hands.  Amazing rebounder. Will score on you inside and out.  Uses power in the post combined with excellent leaping ability.  Has an excellent jump shot with NBA 3-point range. Has the versatility to play both the 3 and the 4 on virtually every team in the league.

Character issues are the biggest question marks. Has been accused of being immature.   Had some off the court issues as a high school player.    As far as basketball goes, there's very little to complain about.  He does need to work on his handle.  Everything else looks great.

One season in Manhattan was all Beasley needed to impress the scouts.
(Brian Spurlock/US Presswire.)


Averaged 28 points, 16 rebounds, 4 assists, 2 steals and 4.5 blocks to help Notre Dame Prep (Mass.) to a 35-3 record and a first-place state finish. Had single-game highs of 64 points, 31 rebounds and 11 assists in 2006-07 season.
Top 2

On talent, he's the best player in college basketball and a virtual lock for either the No. 1 or No. 2 pick in the draft.  The only thing that raises question marks are character questions.  He's been on his best behavior at Kansas State ... will he continue to behave once he has a big, fat guaranteed contract?

It's been a wild ride getting to this pick. Beasley may be the most NBA-ready and talented player in the draft, but it seems as though the Heat had to be talked into drafting him. Even now, some NBA observers still believe that the Heat will continue to explore trades over the next few days and weeks. I think they should keep Beasley. He is such an explosive, versatile scorer, and an excellent rebounder. And I think he's going to play with a chip on his shoulder to prove everyone wrong.
Explosive, versatile scorer and rebounder.

Basketball IQ is off the charts for a big man.  Amazing passer.  Very strong.  Plays physical.  Excellent rebounder.  Skilled both inside and outside.  Excellent range on his jump shot.  Amazing hands. Advanced footwork and low-post moves.  Beautiful baby hook. Master of the shot-fake. Great motor. Tough.  He can throw a perfect strike on a three-quarter court outlet pass.

Lacks ideal size for a center.  Not a great athlete.  Plays below the rim due to a lack of explosive leaping ability. Lacks lateral quickness, making it difficult for him to guard on the perimeter.  Has conditioning issues.   Has had knee problems in the past. Is he just a more skilled version of Tyler Hansbrough?

Helped Lake Oswego (Ore.) to a 26-2 record and state runner-up finish, averaging 33.9 points, 17.0 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 4.2 blocks in the 2006-07 season. Posted career averages of 26.8 points and 14.5 rebounds.
Lottery

Love's game is old-school with a flair for the spectacular. He's an amazing college player, however, NBA scouts worry that his lack of size and athleticism will limit his ceiling in the pros. He's trimmed down and improved his explosiveness in the pros. He's a likely late lottery to mid first-round pick.

Kevin Love has had an immediate impact in Westwood. .
(Stephen Dunn/Getty Images)

Bill Walton.

The Grizzlies have agreed to send the rights to Love to the Wolves. Kevin McHale wanted Love all along, and he picked up a bonus in Mike Miller as part of the deal. The Wolves need help in the low post and Love can provide it right away. Their front line will be undersized, but I can see why they like the deal.
Wolves need help in the low post.

Westbrook might be the top prospect from UCLA.
(Victor Decolongon/Getty Images)

Long, athletic combo guard. Slasher who can get to and finish at the
rim. Explosive leaper. Sees the floor well. Has a solid jump shot. Tenacious defender. Very quick on both ends of the floor. Long arms and great anticipation make him a ball hawk on the defensive end. Excellent speed in the open court. Scouts say he has an excellent work ethic. Seems to improve every time he steps on the floor.

Still learning how to play point guard.  Often plays off the ball with Darren Collison running the point.  Ballhandling needs improvement.  Can get out of control when he takes it to the basket.  Has some range on his jump shot, but doesn't take a lot of 3s.
Lottery
A draft sleeper.  Many NBA scouts believe he's the best prospect on the UCLA team.  He's projected to go anywhere from 8 to 15 in the draft.

Great pick for the Sonics. I know that Sam Presti's heart was with Westbrook. While many think this is too high for him, I don't. I think he has incredible upside and he's a lock to be a great defender. He should develop on the offensive end, too. Overall, he has a chance to be a better version of Rajon Rondo.
Great pick. A lockdown defender.

Big-time scoring guard with excellent size, scoring ability and handle.  Excellent penetrator with quick first step.  Good finisher around the basket.  Has deep range on his jump shot, but streaky.  NBA-ready body. Excellent strength.  Can be a lock-down defender when he wants to be.

Lacks a developed midrange game.  Doesn't always show up on the defensive end.  Has been pegged by scouts as a potential point guard, but seems to lack the decision-making skills or feel to run the point. Has had some off-court issues.  Teams worry that his ego is overinflated with all of the hype since eighth grade.  A year older than everyone else in his class.
Averaged 29.6 points, 5.0 rebounds and 4.9 assists as a high school senior.
Top 10

Mayo began the season as a potential No. 1 pick, dipped into the late lottery after a shaky start but ended the season on a high note.  He may not be the next LeBron, but he does look like he has the tools to be an effective scorer in the league.  He should go somewhere between 3 and 7 in the draft.

O.J. Mayo's draft stock is enjoying a renaissance.
AP Photo/George Nikitin

The Wolves will send the rights to Mayo to Memphis. The Grizzlies have coveted Mayo as a scoring guard who could become a star. The team now has a glut of guards in the backcourt (including Mike Conley, Kyle Lowry and Javaris Crittenton), but it should be able to package one or more of them for a big man to help fill the hole left by Pau Gasol.
Could become a star in Memphis.

Big, athletic center who is has a strong offensive game with the ability to score both inside and out.  Has a great body and uses it well.  Long arms. Smart player who maximizes his strengths.  Has a decent low-post game and has shown an array of basic moves around the basket.  Is a good shooter with the ability to knock down the 18-foot jump shot.  He can even hit a college 3-pointer from time to time.  He is an excellent defender and can be a good shot-blocker at times, though he's inconsistent in that area.  Improving free-throw shooter.
Takes bad shots from time to time.  Although he's a good athlete for his size, he's not particularly explosive. Not a dominant rebounder.

Lopez was part of an impressive twin tandem in Palo Alto.
(AP Photo/George Nikitin)

Brook was suspended from the basketball team because of academic issues and missed the first 9 games of 2007-08 season for Stanford. His twin brother, Robin, also played for Stanford.
Top 10

Brook's stellar play toward the end of his freshman season turned a lot of NBA scouts' heads. His sophomore season was fantastic for Stanford. Although scouts wish he was a little more athletic and a better rebounder, he'll challenge DeAndre Jordan as the first center off the board.

The Nets are doing backflips. They had three guys they really liked in this draft: Kevin Love, Danilo Gallinari and Brook Lopez. They need size and a guy who can score in the low post. I thought Lopez would have been a reach at No. 3, but he's a very solid pick at No. 10. I think this is a very good day for the Nets.
Needed size and got a very solid pick.

Do-it-all combo guard. Big-time range on his jump shot.
Gordon showed he could be an explosive scorer at Indiana.
(AP Photo/Darron Cummings)

Great shooting off the dribble. Excellent finisher at the basket. Great speed. Excellent athlete with explosive leaping ability. Good handle. NBA body. Excellent basketball IQ. Hard worker. Good, physical defender.

He's an undersized 2-guard.  Indiana tried him a little at the point, but it's clear his skills are in the scoring department.  His handle is a little questionable, as are his shot selection and floor vision.  His poor assist-to-turnover ratio doesn't lie here. He hurt his wrist in January and his 3-point shooting percentage plummeted right after that.
Top 10

Coming into the season, many scouts felt that Gordon was as talented as O.J. Mayo and Derrick Rose -- he just didn't generate quite the hype.  As a freshman at Indiana, he lived up to the high expectations as an explosive scorer and excellent defender for most of the season.  He struggled in February and March with his shot thanks to a wrist injury and the departure of head coach Kelvin Sampson.  However, his stock is still high among NBA GMs. On the right team, he can be a superstar.  Right now he looks like a likely Top 10 pick.
A bigger, better version of Ben Gordon

The Clippers have a huge hole in their backcourt and Eric Gordon will really help them there. He can be a star: He is strong, can shoot the long ball and can be a tough defender. I'm not sure he's ready yet, but he'll have to be. With Corey Maggette hitting the free-agent market, the Clippers need Gordon to be good.
A tough defender who can become a star.

All-around skills.  Point-forward mentality.  Beautiful passer.  Excellent basketball IQ.  Smooth.  Excellent slasher to the basket.  Good athlete, though not an exceptional one.  Good shooter, especially from midrange.
He lacks explosiveness. Although he's not slow footed, he's not exactly quick either.  May be a little too unselfish.  Questions about his long-range shooting.

Gallinari could join Bargnani as a high NBA draft pick.
(IPA Photo/imago/Icon SMI )

Gallinari has declared for the 2008 NBA draft.

Plays for Armani Jeans, Milano in the Italian League.
Averaged 14.9 ppg and 4.2 rpg in 31 mpg in Euroleague play this season. Averaging 17.5 ppg and 4.8 rpg in the Italian league. His father was a star player in Italy.
Lottery

Many in Italy feel he's a better long-term prospect than Andrea Bargnani.  Right now his game is more suited for Europe, but the Toni Kukoc comparisons are inevitable.  He's having a big season this year and more and more scouts are saying that he's a potential lottery pick.

It was meant to be. Mike D'Antoni once played with his father in Italy, and he's the perfect forward for D'Antoni's system. He's tough, he can run the floor, he handles the ball and he shoots it with range. He's more like Dirk Nowitzki or Toni Kukoc than fellow Italian Andrea Bargnani.
He's perfect for D'Antoni's system.

DeAndre Jordan's talent pushes him high up many draft boards.
(Chris McGrath/Getty Images)

Big-time athlete. Great body. Very long. Explosive leaper. Excellent
rebounder and shot-blocker. Great hands. Strong finisher around the basket. Runs the floor well. Very quick for a big guy. Developing hook shot in the paint.

Scouts wonder about his motor. Doesn't always play hard.  Disappears for stretches.  Still fairly raw offensively.  Gets most of points off dunks.  No face-the-basket game. Needs to add core strength to hold his position better in the paint. Horrific free-throw shooter. Poor passer.  Collects an unusually low amount of steals.  Poor production in the second half of the season.
Averaged 19 points, 14 rebounds and 6 blocks for Christian Life Center in Houston as a senior.
Lottery

On talent and physical ability, he's got the makings of a Top 5 pick.  Jordan would be the No. 1 pick in the draft if he were producing anywhere near the numbers of the guys ranked ahead of him. However, his poor second half has hurt his stock somewhat.  While it's difficult to pinpoint his position exactly, it's hard to see him slipping out of the lottery.
Dwight Howard

We knew DeAndre Jordan was sliding, but this is a little ridiculous. He's huge and athletic, and he played well when he got minutes at Texas A&M. NBA scouts would have ranked him as one of the top-five prospects in 2009. At No. 35, there is no risk and only upside for the Clippers. They have to be thrilled.
Huge athlete with a lot of upside.

Solid big man with great size, strength and length. Can rebound, block shots and play physical defense.  Hard worker who improved from his freshman to junior seasons.  Good hands.  Nice footwork in the paint. Good low-post passer.  Decent range on his jump shot.  Good basketball IQ. Relatively young for a college senior.

He's not a great athlete.  Lumbering isn't the right word, but he does play fairly robotically.  A lack of explosiveness or quickness to his game will hurt him at the next level.  Not much of a rebounder considering his size.

Hibbert's not very athletic, but he does have some big-man skills.
(James Lang/US Presswire)

Hibbert declared for the 2007 NBA draft, but withdrew before the deadline
despite the fact that he looked like a lock for the Top 15 picks in the draft.
Mid to late first round

He's been all over the boards with scouts over the past few years.  They love his size and potential, but he seems to have leveled out as 13-point, 7-rebound a night guy.  That's caused his stock to dip a bit.  While a few lottery teams will take a look, he's looking more like a mid first rounder right now.

Toronto is making this pick for the Pacers. This is an interesting pick for Indiana. He does add a low post scorer and give the Pacers much-needed size. But his lack of athleticism and rebounding make me wonder if this was the best pick for Indiana. I think I would've grabbed Darrell Arthur here. He seems to be a better fit for Jim O'Brien's system.
Non-athlete will be shipped to Indiana.

Randolph reminds some of Chris Bosh.
(Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

A super athletic big man with a long wingspan. Explosive leaper.
Skilled. Can score with his back to the basket or by sinking a 15-footer. Has excellent speed for a big man. Runs the floor very well. Has shown that he can be a serious force on the boards and as a shot-blocker.

Lacks strength.  Needs to add a lot of muscle to his frame.  He gets pushed around on both ends of the floor.  While he has a reliable outside shot, he doesn't have deep range.  Poor free-throw shooter.  Still raw with his low-post moves.
Lottery
Randolph generated significant buzz from trusted NBA scouts during the season.  However his weight and so-so workouts have hurt his draft stock.  He's no longer a lock for the Top 10
Brandan Wright

Interesting pick for the Warriors. At this point you go with the best talent available, and I think, as far as upside goes, that was Randolph. Here's the problem: They drafted the same kind of guy last year, Brandan Wright, another super-athletic freshman forward drafted on the basis of potential. What do they do now that they have both of them?
Went with best available player.

Quick, athletic point guard with excellent court leadership skills. Can make passes
few NBA point guards can pull off. Does an excellent job of probing and keeping his dribble until the right pass opens up. Excellent shooter with legit NBA 3-point range. Shows the right balance between scoring and getting his teammates involved. Gets to the free-throw line and sinks his shots. NBA body. Excellent finisher in traffic.

The biggest knock is his size.  He's probably closer to 5-foot-10 than 6-feet.  Has been a little turnover prone this season.  Tries to do too much which forces him to take bad shots. Can be too unselfish at times.

Augustin is a huge fan of Steve Nash and it shows in his game.
Augustin had a strong sophomore season.
(Brian Spurlock/US Presswire)
Lottery

Augustin was one of the two or three best freshmen point guards in the country last season.  With Kevin Durant gone, Augustin stepped up and helped Texas have a great season -- better in fact than the it did last year with Durant on board.  He continues to develop as a leader and his combination of quickness and shooting ability make him one of the best point guard prospects in the draft.  He was dominated by Derrick Rose in the tournament, but who wasn't?  He should go somewhere between No. 7 and No. 12 on draft night.

A little bit of a surprise. We've been hearing all day that the Bobcats are shopping Raymond Felton. I guess this confirms it. They passed on a need (Brook Lopez) to get Augustin. He's an upgrade over Felton, so it's hard to criticize the Bobcats. Augustin has a chance to be special. The Blazers and Kings wanted him and have to be crushed right now.
Upgrade over Felton. A chance to be special.

Rush is athletic, has an NBA body and shoots the ball really well.  Has long arms and good strength. He's a very versatile player who could play both the 2 and 3 in the pros.  Has a maturity about him and is an excellent 3-point shooter.

Can be too unselfish at times.  Seems to fade into the background at times. Needs to work on his ballhandling.  He still struggles to create his own shot.  .  Scouts worry about a broken elbow he had as a kid.  Rush is unable to straighten his right arm because of the injury.

Rush enters the draft with a national title on his resume.
(Douglas Jones/Icon SMI)

Rush has declared for the 2008 NBA draft. Because this is the second time he's declared for the draft, he must stay in and will hire an agent, ending his college eligibility.

Rush declared but withdrew from the 2007 NBA draft after
hurting his ACL preparing for the Orlando predraft camp. Rush put his name in the NBA draft in 2005, played in the Chicago predraft camp, but withdrew his name after he wasn't promised to be taken in the first round.
Mid to late first round

Rush finally seems like he's fully recovered from his ACL injury and put up impressive numbers at Kansas in the second half of the season.  He may be one of the more underrated players in the draft.  Right now he looks like a mid to late first-round pick.

The Blazers will send the rights to Rush, Jarrett Jack and Josh McRoberts to the Pacers for the rights to Bayless and Ike Diogu. I think this is a great pick for the Pacers. Rush should be a great fit in the backcourt with T.J. Ford because he defends, shoots the ball and has great size. Rush is one of the most NBA-ready players in the draft.
Dealt to Pacers. Is NBA ready.
A big, athletic center who is very active on the glass.  Good shot-blocker.  Good lateral quickness.  Gets up the floor well. Excellent defender. Motor runs very high. Tough.
Unlike his brother, Brook, he's not nearly as gifted an offensive player.  He struggles to score in ways other than dunks and off of offensive boards.  Poor free-throw shooter.

Robin announced that he was declaring for the 2008 NBA draft and hiring an agent, ending his college eligibility.

Has a twin brother, Brook, who also played at Stanford.
Will Robin Lopez' draft stock soar?
(AP Photo/Marcio Jose Sanchez)
Lottery to mid first round

He's not as talented as his brother, Brook, but he too has NBA potential. He's really started to come on late for the Cardinal and is even starting to score more.  He'll have appeal to NBA teams looking for a big defensive stopper.  Right now he's a mid to late first-round pick.

Solid pick for the Suns. It's clear Mike D'Antoni is no longer in Phoenix. Lopez brings energy and defense, but he's an offensive liability. Once Brandon Rush was off the board, Phoenix felt Lopez was best fit for its needs.
Brings energy and defense to the floor.
Super-athletic big man with great size and length.  Explosive leaper.  Great shot-blocker.  Strong rebounder.  Has a nice jump shot out to about 18 feet.
Still learning the game.  Doesn't have a great feel yet playing with his teammates.  Most of his stuff is done one-on-one.  Still learning how to play in the paint on the offensive end.

Plays for CB L'Hospitalet in the Spanish second league.
Serge Ibaka of the Congo is gaining experience in Spain.
(Courtesy USA Basketball)
Late first to early second

Ibaka got some hype this summer at an Adidas camp and international scouts will follow him very closely in the Spanish league.  He says he'll enter his name in the draft this year, but it may be a little premature until we see how he responds to better competition in the Spanish league.  He has the raw materials to be a lottery pick, but scouts still have to figure out if he has the skills to survive in the league.

We've seen this one coming for a while -- the Sonics have been keying on him. He's one of the best athletes in the draft, but he's very, very raw. He'll go back to Spain and continue to develop, but down the road he could become an interesting prospect.
One of the best athletes in the draft.

Courtney Lee is that rare college senior who could be a first-round pick.
(Brian Spurlock/US PRESSWIRE)

Excellent shooter who can also get his shot by putting the ball
on the floor and getting to the basket. Has 3-point range on his jumper but is at his best as a midrange shooter. Good athlete. Nice strength and NBA body.
He doesn't contribute a lot in rebounds, assists or at the defensive end.  Has been criticized for not being aggressive in the past, though that seemed to have changed this season.
Late first to early second

Lee has been on NBA scouts' radar all year.  However, his so-so performance in the NCAA tournament left many of them ambivalent.  He's one of the few seniors in this draft with a legit shot at the first round.

The Magic need a scoring 2-guard who can shoot the basketball. They thought J.J. Redick was that guy, but he wasn't. Lee is solid. I don't think he'll be a star, but he's proven and ready. It's interesting that, given the Magic's needs in the post, they didn't grab Darrell Arthur.
Won't be a star but proven and ready.

Athletic big man with an excellent face-the-basket game.  Long arms and explosive leaping ability make him an excellent shot-blocker and a good rebounder.  Is developing a low-post game, but is still very raw.  Has a reliable midrange jump shot and even some college 3-point range.  Has the ability to create his own shot off the dribble.  Good motor for a big man.  Could be a 4 or a 5 in the league.
Still developing, especially as a low-post player on the offensive end.  Needs to add strength and weight, though it looks like he has the frame to do it.  Poor free-throw shooter.

With strong hoop lineage, McGee is making a name for himself in Reno.
(AP Photo/Kevin Clifford)



His father, George Montgomery, was drafted by the Blazers
in the second round of the 1985 NBA Draft. His mother, Pamela McGee, played and coached in the WNBA.
Lottery to mid first round

Right now he's one of the biggest sleepers in the draft.  He's still a year or two away from being ready for the NBA, but his improvement this season has been dramatic.   He could go anywhere from the late lottery  to late first round.   Right now we have him somewhere in the middle,  
but with great workouts, he has the potential to crack the lottery.   You aren't going to find many prospects with his combination of size,
length, athleticism and basketball skills.

I'm not a huge fan of this pick, especially with a proven guy like Darrell Arthur on the board. McGee is a physical specimen, very long and athletic, and he has some skills. But he's very soft and looks like he's years away. He reminds me of Andray Blatche.
Very long and athletic, but very soft.
Scoring combo guard is an excellent athlete.  Good shooter, with NBA range, though he doesn't take a lot of 3-pointers.  Excellent getting to the line. Efficient scorer.
Can be turnover prone.  Lacks ideal size at the 2.  A bit of a tweener.

George Hill hasn't played in the big-time spotlight much.
(AP Photo/Terry Gilliam)
Second round to undrafted
A few scouts feel that Hill is a sleeper.  A great performance at Orlando (if he can get in) will help him as he doesn't get the exposure of other players.  A possible second-round pick.

You have to love the Spurs. They always march to the beat of a different drummer. I sort of like this pick because I think he's a guy who can really play -- and play both the 1 and 2. But is he really better than Mario Chalmers? I don't think so. I don't want to second-guess one of the best-drafting teams in the NBA, but I think Chalmers will be a better NBA player.
A bit of a tweener. Like Chalmers better.

Silky-smooth swing man.  Has a high basketball IQ and can play several positions on the floor.   Long arms.  Very athletic.  Excellent defender with quick hands and feet. Beginning to show nice range on his jump shot.  Has developed a pro body.
Needs experience at the top level.  Is known for disappearing from time to time on the court.  Lacks consistent aggressiveness.  Needs to work on his ballhandling skills.

Plays for LeMans in France. Averaged 8.5 ppg and 3.5 rpg in 26 mpg in Euroleague play this year. Batum stopped participating in a workout with the Toronto Raptors on June 19th after a stress echo test -- a treadmill test that measures the health of the heart -- came back in the "borderline" area. His agent said that the problem isn't serious.
Batum is held in very high regard by some international scouts.
(AP Photo/David Vincent)
Mid to late first round

His dominance at the 2007 Nike Hoop Summit  had many believing he would be a lottery pick.  However his play for LeMans this season has been uneven.  He can be spectacular at times, then disappear at others.  A concern over the health of Batum's heart could factor into where he's drafted.  Batum had an issue with a stress echo test in Toronto.  His agent says that the issue isn't serious, but it could scare off teams thinking about taking him early.
Mickael Pietrus

The Rockets have agreed to trade this pick to the Blazers. While Batum didn't fare well in John Hollinger's Euroleague translations, he has tremendous upside as a wing, and the Blazers are intrigued. He has all the tools, but does he have the drive? I spoke with Portland GM Kevin Pritchard tonight and he says he thinks Batum will actually sign with the Blazers this year.
Has upside. Traded to Portland.

Excellent offensive player who can get it done both inside and out.   Especially lethal from the perimeter.   Shooting better than 40 percent from 3-point territory.   Good rebounder.   Nice touch on the inside.  Excellent passer.  Good basketball IQ.  Has long arms which makes him play bigger than he is.

Not a great athlete.  He's not a stiff by any means, but he doesn't have that freakish athleticism that NBA scouts look for in big men.  He's going to need to add strength to play inside at the next level. So-so defender lacks the lateral agility to guard quicker players, and can get bruised by bigger opponents inside.
Anderson has declared for the 2008 NBA draft, but hasn't hired an agent, preserving his college eligibility.
Late first to early second

Anderson wasn't highly touted coming out of high school and took many scouts by surprise with his stellar play his freshman season  As a sophomore, he's proven that he's going to be a consistent go-to guy for Cal.  Right now he's firmly on the first-round bubble.

Ryan Anderson is still eligible to return to Berkeley.
(Lisa Blumenfeld/Getty Images)

Troy Murphy.

We knew the Nets were high on two guys -- Hickson and Anderson. Anderson is a face-the-basket 4 who can shoot the ball -- kind of like Yi Jianlian. He's talented, but I think I would have grabbed DeAndre Jordan here.
A talented four who can shoot the ball.

Arthur has a high ceiling when it comes to potential.
(Jamie Squire/Getty Images)

Long, athletic forward who can play both the 3 and the 4. He
has a nice midrange jump shot and combines that with an array of nice post moves. Very agile player who can get up and down the floor. Excellent rebounder and defender. Can defend both the 3 and the 4. Good shot-blocker.

Needs to add weight and muscle to his thin frame.  A bit of a tweener right now.  Has been very inconsistent. Doesn't possess real NBA 3-point range on his jumper.  Just a so-so rebounder. Still working on his ballhandling.  A black hole.  Once he gets the ball, he's going to shoot it.
Lottery to mid first round

On potential, he's one of the top dozen prospects in the country, however his sophomore performance was a little disappointing until the NCAA title game.  When Arthur is engaged, he looks like a lottery pick.  But his tendency to disappear and his lackluster rebounding now have him on the lottery bubble.

The Blazers have agreed to trade Arthur and the 33rd pick to the Rockets. Houston then then shipped Arthur to Memphis. When the Rockets drafted Batum, I questioned it. He measured out terribly statistically under John Hollinger's formula and the Rockets are stat geniuses. Lo and behold, they swap the pick for Arthur, whom Hollinger listed as the fifth-best prospect. Yes, teams were worried about a kidney issue. But I've talked to two teams, and I'm told it's not a big deal. He has a chance to be an Antawn Jamison-type player.
Possibly a steal. Most traded on draft night.

Huge body with good athleticism and strength.   Good low-post scorer.  Efficient.  Quick in the paint.  Impressive low-post moves for a sophomore. Good defender and shot-blocker.  Excellent rebounder.  Tough.

His conditioning is still an issue.  He needs to work on his jump shot.  He doesn't have a great face the basket game. Might be a little undersized to play center in the NBA. Scouts question his work ethic.

Speights has declared for the 2008 NBA draft, but hasn't hired an agent, preserving his college eligibility.

Speight's per-40-minute numbers as a freshman were off the charts. He
Speights could join a recent flood of Gators into the NBA..
(Jimmy DeFlippo/US Presswire)

averaged 28.3 points and 18.2 rebounds.
Lottery to mid first round

With Al Horford and Joakim Noah in the NBA, a lot fell on Speight's large shoulders at Florida -- and he delivered.  Like Horford and Noah, he did big things in around 24 minutes per game.  A likely late lottery to mid first-round pick.

I like this pick for Philly. Speights has a lot of talent and he fits a need for Philly. He's an excellent offensive player who can score in the post and facing the basket, and he can rebound. He is kind of a poor man's Elton Brand.
A lot of talent here and fills a need.
Long, physical big man who is excellent on the offensive boards and as a shot-blocker.  Decent athlete.  Good lateral quickness and leaping ability make him an intimidating defender.
For a European big man -- he isn't very skilled.  Gets most of his points on putbacks and dunks.  No jump shot or offensive moves to speak of.

Plays for Fenerbache Ulker in the Euroleague. Averaged 7.8 ppg and 5.5 rpg in 18 mpg on 60 percent shooting.
Asik, right, has shown potential in limited minutes.
(Sezayi Erken/AFP/Getty Images)
Late first to early second
He's only played 15 game in the Euroleague ... but was enough to get him on just about every international scouts radar.   A likely late-first to early-second round selection.

The Blazers agreed to send Asik to the Bulls for three future second-round picks. I think Asik could be one of the steals of the second round ... if he ever comes over. He's a hyperactive rebounder and shot-blocker with good athleticism. John Hollinger said his numbers suggest he should've been a top-10 pick. He's a talent, but he may be in Turkey for the next few years developing his game.
Will develop in Europe. Could be a steal.

J.J. Hickson looked impressive in Raleigh.
(AP Photo/Al Goldis)

Athletic big man with an NBA body. Explosive leaper. Physical.
Good finisher around the basket. Does most of his damage inside the key. Can hit the midrange jumper. Can put the ball on the floor and create his own shot. Excellent rebounder. Good shot-blocker.
Still lacks some basketball IQ.  Post moves are raw.  Not especially quick.
Hickson has declared for the 2008 NBA draft but hasn't hired an agent,  preserving his college eligibility.
Mid to late first round

A rising young player who has had a stellar freshman season for NC State.  Teams love his body and athleticism.  One of this year's draft sleepers.  A mid-first-round pick if he  stays in the draft.  A potential lottery pick in 2009.

I'm surprised they passed on local hero Kosta Koufos of Ohio State. But I do like Hickson, who's a sleeper. He's strong and athletic and he can score in multiple ways. He was 12-for-12 from the field in his first college game.
A sleeper among the freshmen in draft.

Big-time scoring guard who loves to attack the defense.   Excellent athlete with explosive leaping ability.  Quick first step allows him to get into the teeth of the defense.  Good shooter who gets excellent elevation on his jump shot.  Has good floor vision and passing ability.
A bit of a tweener.  Can play the point, but prefers to score.  Can play out of control at times.  Poor rebounder.  Doesn't collect steals at a high rate despite his quickness and athleticism.

Is Jerryd Bayless the thinking man's Monta Ellis?
(AP Photo/Jerry Lai)



As a high school senior in 2006-07, averaged 33.2 points, 7.8 rebounds,
6.1 assists and 2.0 steals, and shot 89.1 percent from the free-throw line to help St. Mary's (Ariz.) to a 19-13 record and state runner-up finish.
Top 10

Bayless' combination of elite athleticism, shooting ability and quickness make him an excellent NBA prospect. One scout compared him to a better shooting, more intelligent Monta Ellis, another to Gilbert Arenas. He's projected in the mid lottery.
Gilbert Arenas

Bayless really slid in the draft, which makes him a great value here. Why would the Pacers draft another point guard after trading for T.J. Ford? Because they're sending Bayless to the Blazers for the No. 13 pick, Jarrett Jack and Josh McRoberts. So how will Bayless fit with the Blazers? He isn't the pure point guard that Kevin Pritchard pined for, but he's an excellent scorer and competitor, and an upgrade over Jack.
Shipped to Portland. Upgrade over Jack.

A great NCAA Finals really showcased Chalmers' game.
(AP Photo/Eric Gay)

The complete package. Chalmers is a sweet-shooting point guard who knows how to run a team and plays excellent defense. Picks up a lot of steals. Very efficient. A clutch shooter. Fearless.

Is he a true point guard?  Many see him as more of a combo guard due to his lack of ballhandling skills and so-so athleticism.  If that's the case, he lacks the ideal size and athleticism for a 2-guard.
Chalmers has declared for the 2008 NBA draft, but won't hire an agent, preserving his college eligibility.
Mid to late first round

Chalmers has been a huge part of KU's success, but his draft future is still far from certain. His play in the NCAA tournament was stellar, but does he have what it takes to be anything more than just a backup in the NBA?  He's gotten enough buzz to propel him into the first round.   But how high?  A couple of teams have him in the late lottery.  Others in the mid to late first round.

The Timberwolves are selecting Chalmers on behalf of the Miami Heat, according to a league source. Pat Riley wanted a point guard, and he got one. In fact, Chalmers is one of the most NBA-ready guards in the draft. He can shoot, he can defend and he's a clutch player. He's kind of a poor man's O.J. Mayo. Great draft night for Miami.
NBA-ready guard who can shoot.

Long, super athletic forward who can score inside and outside.  Explosive leaper. Gets to the basket and is a strong finisher.  Is big enough to post up smaller defenders and has a great touch around the basket.  High basketball IQ.  Very good passer for a big man.  Very quick laterally.
Struggles with his ballhandling.   A streaky 3-point shooter.  Still developing ... needs to improve his basketball IQ.

Alexander is a NBA draft sleeper.
(Rich Kane/Icon SMI )
Lottery to mid first round

He's an intriguing prospect.  Several scouts have him as a late lottery to mid first round pick based on potential.  Others think he needs his senior season to work on his jump shot and ballhandling.  He finished the season very strong.  He's testing the waters without hiring an agent.  If he works out well,  someone could bite in the late lottery to mid first round.

The Bucks have loved Joe Alexander for weeks. But where will he play? Milwaukee just traded for Richard Jefferson. I think the Bucks have more pressing needs now at the 4 and in the backcourt. We'll have to see how this plays out. But the Bucks wanted a talent with lots of upside, and Alexander has that.
Had more pressing needs to fill.

A long, athletic jump shooter who can play both the 3 and 4.  Excellent midrange game.  Has improved his 3-point shooting -- though it's still streaky. Has the ability to put the ball on the floor and take his man to the basket.  Explosive leaper.  Has turned into a leader on his team.  Solid rebounder.
Needs to add strength.  A bit of a tweener right now.  Poor decision making and shot selection.  Doesn't always look like he knows what he's doing out there.

Donte Greene had an immediate impact in Syracuse.
Chris McGrath/Getty Images



Averaged 18.4 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 2.1 steals and 4.3 blocks
as a senior in 2006-07, helping Towson to a 32-6 record and to its second consecutive Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association A Conference and Baltimore Catholic League titles.
Lottery to mid first round

Versatile forward got off to a hot start for Syracuse.  He cooled a bit in the second half of the season, but scouts are still high on his long-term prospects. While he still needs to refine his game, there's no questioning that he's one of the best talents in the draft. A potential lottery pick.
Marvin Williams

Another value pick. Lots of scouts compare him to Rashard Lewis. Greene is a perimeter shooter who lacks a position or real game right now, and I'm not sure how he fits on Memphis, which already has Rudy Gay. But the Grizzlies have been shopping this pick, so I wouldn't be surprised to see Greene wearing another hat later tonight.
Good value. A solid perimeter shooter.

Skilled big man with excellent size, length and good body.  Has a 7-foot-4 inch wingspan. Has great strength and good, but not great athleticism for his size.  Has offensive skills both inside and out.  Nice moves and footwork in the paint.  Excellent midrange shooter with very consistent range out to 18 feet.  Has 3-point range as well, but is much more streaky from there.   He lacks the explosiveness to be an elite shot-blocker, but his timing is good.  Decent rebounder.  Good passer out of double-teams.  Is pretty mobile for a big man.

Needs polish and experience.  Can be a disinterested defender at times.  Lacks aggressiveness at times.  Lacks lateral quickness. Can sometimes lose his confidence and then his game falls apart.  Needs to be able to handle contact in the paint better.

Koufos earned an NIT title in his first season in Columbus.
(AP Photo/Terry Gilliam)

Koufos has declared for the 2008 NBA draft, and has hired agent Mark Termini, ending his college eligibility.


Averaged 26.5 points, 13 rebounds, 3.5 blocks or 1.4 steals in the U-18
European Championships this summer.
Lottery to mid first round

His excellent play in the summer for the Greek national team seems to have only carried over so far.   Scouts still think Koufos is a terrific prospect with great size, basketball IQ and the ability to stretch the defense with a silky smooth jumper.  But his inconsistency against college big men, lack of rebounding and so-so shot-blocking numbers all have scouts saying he may need to wait another year if he really wants to strike gold in the  lottery.  Nevertheless, Koufos has declared for the draft and projects as a potential lottery pick.
Darko Milicic

Great value pick for the Jazz at No. 23. He could be the second coming of Mehmet Okur -- a sweet-shooting big man who can play inside and outside. If Koufos had stayed in school, he would have been projected as a top-10 pick in 2009, so I don't think the Jazz could have done much better at 23.
Great value. A sweet shooting big man.

picks.tradeNote: from OKC via WSH and PHI

analysis.text:
Big man, with excellent length and an NBA body.
Jason Thompson aims to go from a New Jersey mid-major to the NBA..
(AP Photo/Mike Groll)

Thompson has the ability to score with his back to the basket. Excellent rounder who uses strength and position to grab rebounds. Long arms allow him to be a good shot-blocker. Not a great athlete but solid. Has some range on his jumper.
He's still very raw, especially offensively.  Can get careless with the ball.  Often tries to do too much and gets frustrated when he or his team is struggling. Big fish in a small pond.
Late first to early second
He's not great, but he has size and an NBA body.  That will give him a serious look by NBA scouts in the late first to early second round.

Wow! This is the biggest surprise of the draft. Though the Warriors liked him at No. 14, we had Thompson projected as a late first-round pick. He's solid, but that's it. There are much better players on the board here. Perhaps the Kings were shell-shocked after losing out on Bayless and Augustin, the two point guards they wanted.
Biggest surprise of the draft.

picks.tradeNote: from WSH via OKC and HOU

analysis.text: Strong low-post player who uses strength, position and some explosiveness to finish around the basket.    Aggressive scorer and defender.  Has nice touch around the basket and a decent close-range jumper out to about 10 feet.

Not particularly skilled.  Not much of a dribbler or a passer.  He just catches in the paint and scores.  Doesn't have great footwork, his game is mostly power.  A decent athlete, but just so-so lateral quickness.  His basketball IQ is so-so.  Lacks the ideal size for a NBA center .. he's closer to 6-10 than his listed 6-11.

Plays for KK Partizan in the Adriatic League and the Euroleague.
Power is the name of Nikola Pekovic's game.
(Andrej Isakovic/AFP/Getty Images)

Averaging 17.6 ppg and 8 rpg in 28 mpg in the first 15 Euroleague Games.
Second round to undrafted

He is dominating in both the Euroleague and the Adriatic league at the start of the season.  That's turning some heads.  He's not your typical Euro big man ... but in his case that's a good thing. Worries about him signing a long-term contract with Panathinikos have scouts wondering if he'll ever come to the NBA to play.

This one we've been hearing for a while. The Wolves have one of the top international scouts in the NBA, Pete Philo, who also runs the Reebok Eurocamp, and he's had an eye on Pekovic for a while. He was the most dominant international player in the draft, with an awesome performance in the Euroleague. He's a tough, bruising big man. But he just signed a huge professional contract in Greece and won't be in the NBA anytime soon.
Most dominant international player in draft.

Super long, athletic forward who does a little of everything.  He crashes the glass, is a lock-down defender and has an emerging offensive game.  Quickness and athleticism make him a great slasher and finisher. Great motor on both ends of the floor.

Still learning the game.  Not a great shooter.  His form is OK, but he really doesn't have long range on his jumper.  No real offensive moves in the post to speak of.  Is mistake prone and streaky, but most scouts attribute that to his relative lack of experience.
Is a prince in Cameroon.
Late first to early second

His play during the NCAA tournament as a freshman made him a top prospect.  He has the energy and athleticism that every coach loves.  But his disappointing play through his sophomore  and junior season hurt his stock.  A strong NCAA tournament this season has scouts interested again, but right now he projects as a late first to second-round pick.

Luc Richard Mbah a Moute can bring down the house with his athleticism.
(Lisa Blumenfeld/Getty Images)

Ron Artest.

Do you think maybe the Bucks thought that they needed help at small forward? The Bucks acquired their third small forward of the day. Mbah a Moute is a terrific defender who is a little like a bigger Bruce Bowen. He'll never wow you offensively, but he should be in the league a long time.
A terrific defender. Think Bruce Bowen.

Smooth swingman who excels at getting to the basket.   Good quickness.  Good at breaking down defenders off the dribbler.  Good finisher around the basket.   Good midrange game.  Good ball handler.  Excellent basketball IQ.  Wiry strong.  Good defender who really can harass an opponent.

Needs to improve his long-range jump shot.  He shot the ball consistently from 3-point range this year, but he didn't take a lot of them.  Could add some bulk to his frame.  For someone with such good ball skills, he rarely gives up the rock.  A good athlete, but not a great one.

Chris Douglas-Roberts is one of several Memphis players with legitimate draft hopes.
(Marvin Gentry/US Presswire )

Douglas-Roberts has declared for the 2008 NBA draft and will hire an agent, ending his college eligibility.
Mid to late first round

Douglas-Roberts is one of the more underrated players in the country.  He really benefited from having Derrick Rose in the lineup with hm this year.  It took some pressure off him as a go-to scorer and gave him a point guard who can set him up for easy shots.  For someone so productive, scouts have been a little mixed on him.  He's a likely mid-to-late first-round pick

The Nets make what could be their best pick of the night. I don't love Chris Douglas-Roberts, but he can score and is one of the best slashers in the draft. For a team that could use more juice in the backcourt, this is a fantastic value.
Fantastic value. Great slashing player.

He's a highly-skilled big man.  Used to be a point guard and has excellent  ballhandling and passing ability.  Nice midrange jump shot.  Has good footwork around the basket and a variety of low-post moves.  Good athlete.
He's rail thin.  Needs another 20 pounds on his frame.  His lack of strength limits his effectiveness in the post on both ends of the floor.  Gets in foul trouble a lot.

As Croatian sensations go, Tomic is rising to great heights.
(AP Photo/Filip Horvat)

Tomic has declared for the 2008 NBA Draft

Averaged 13 points and 7.2 rebounds on 61 percent shooting in the Adriatic League this season. Tomic declared for the 2007 NBA draft, but withdrew after a dispute with his Croatian club, KK Zagreb.
Late first to early second

Tomic is big-time prospect.  He has a rare combination of size, skill and athletic ability.  And he's really starting to live up to his potential in the Adriatic League. But he may be another year away.  His body really needs to fill out before he can even think about the NBA.  A possible late first-round pick for a team that wants to keep him in Europe another year or two.

Another great pick for the Jazz. They seriously considered drafting Tomic with the No. 23 pick and get him here at No. 42. Tomic is one of the most skilled bigs in this draft, but he needs to get much, much stronger. He's been very productive in Europe but his body just isn't ready for the NBA. He'll return to Croatia for the next few years.
Needs to get stronger. But good value.

D.J. White might measure up in the NBA.
(AJ Mast/Icon SMI)

White has hit the weight room and his body is
looking stronger than ever. He is a big-time rebounder and excellent defender with the ability to score both inside and out. His long wingspan and added strength should help him. He's a good athlete with good leaping ability. He has excellent hands and strength underneath the basket.

Scouts think he's much closer to 6-foot-7 than his listed height of 6-foot-9.  While White possesses a decent outside shot, he doesn't use it as much as he should.  Relies on muscle and athleticism more than actual basketball moves in the paint. Injuries have pushed him off the radar screen for the past few seasons
Late first to early second
White is finally healthy and had a stellar senior season in Indiana.  If he can measure anywhere close to the 6-9 he's listed at he's going to get a look from NBA scouts in the late first round.

Detroit is selecting White for the Seattle SuperSonics, a Pistons source told me. The Pistons will get two of the Sonics' second-rounders -- the 32nd and 46th picks. This is a very solid pick for the Sonics. White is an excellent rebounder and a good low post scorer. He's also young for a senior. He helps the Sonics get tougher up front.
Rebounder, low post scorer dealt to Sonics.

picks.tradeNote: from MEM via ATL and UTA

analysis.text: Super long, wiry forward with good athleticism.  Amazing 7-foot-8 wingspan. Very skilled for a big man.  Nice form on his jump shot.  Prefers to play facing the basket.  Good moves in the paint.  Solid rebounder and shot-blocker.

Very weak for the position.  Needs to continue to add weight and muscle to that frame.  Inexperienced.  Hasn't seen much action at the highest level of play in Europe.  Scouts have had to settle for watching him in junior tournaments and the Hoop Summit.

Ajinca declared for the 2008 NBA draft.

Alexis Ajinca could be the next NBA player from France.
(Sam Forencich/NBAE via Getty Images)

Plays for Hyeres-Toulon in France. Scored 13 points and grabbed 7 rebounds in the 2008 Nike Hoop Summit for the International team.
Late first  to early second

He's an intriguing prospect for down the road ....  Until he starts to fill out and gets more playing time, there isn't much to draft him on except his raw potential  Of course, NBA teams do that all the time, and Ajinca has the talent.  He's a first-round bubble guy right now.
A poor man's LaMarcus Aldridge

Ajinca is 20 years old and averaged 5 ppg in France. In the history of the NBA draft, has there ever been a player who averaged 5 ppg or less who turned into a decent player? Ajinca was a workout warrior, dominating some of the other big men in the past few weeks. And he has great size and skills. But can he turn them into production on the court? He'll likely stay in France to develop.
Great size and skills. A workout warrior.
Very quick and athletic guard.  Explosive.  Long arms. Excellent ability to change directions.  Very good ball handler.  A good shooter and good finisher around the basket.
Can play out of control at times.  Turnover prone.  Still streaky from 3-point range.  Character issues related to his dismissal from Iowa State.

Taylor spent two years at Chipola JC. Then he transferred to Iowa State.
Mike Taylor impressed at the NBA pre-draft camp in Orlando.
(AP Photo/Reinhold Matay)

After one season, Taylor was kicked out of school. He then played a year in the NBDL where he averaged 14.5 ppg for the Idaho Stampede.
Second round to undrafted
Taylor's excellent performance at the Orlando pre-draft camp combined with a solid year in the D-League has made him a hot name in the second round.

The Blazers have agreed to trade this pick to the Clippers for a future second-round pick. Taylor is a very athletic point guard who played well at the Orlando pre-draft camp. Character issues pushed him out at Iowa State and into the D-League this year, where he put up impressive numbers.
Athletic point guard. Has character issues.

picks.tradeNote: from NO via BOS, DET and POR

analysis.text: Super athletic, versatile wing is a beast when he puts the ball on the floor and gets to the rim.  Jumps out of the gym. Very quick. Good handle.  Sees the floor well. Excellent perimeter shooter with deep range. Already possesses an NBA body.

Three ACL injuries, one to his right knee in 2003 and one to his left in 2007, are the biggest knocks right now.  He's struggled to lose all the weight he gained after his last injury and still doesn't seem 100 percent recovered. There was a time when scouts wondered a little about his ballhandling, but they say he's improved that weakness.

Walker has declared for the 2008 NBA draft, but hasn't hired an agent, preserving his college eligibility.

Walker ruptured his ACL in early January 2007 and missed the remainder of his freshman season.
Mid to late first round

Walker's second ACL injury ended all the talk about him being a top-5 pick.  Given that Walker's freakish athleticism was his greatest strength, the ACL injury permanently damaged his stock.  His strong play through part of the second half of the season helped put him in the first-round discussion.

Walker's game was on full display with the Wildcats.
(Peter Aiken/WireImage.com)

Vince Carter before the ACL injury.

The Wizards traded this pick to the Celtics. Nice pickup for Boston, considering that last year he was projected as a lottery pick before suffering another ACL injury. He's still very explosive, with an NBA body. If Walker can stay healthy, the Celtics just got much more athletic on the wings with the addition of him and Giddens.
A nice pickup if he can stay healthy.

Strong combo guard is difficult to keep out of the lane. Excellent ball hander.  Aggressive scorer.  Very tough. Excellent rebounder for a guard. Good defender.  Can play some point guard.  Good athlete.
Turnover prone.  More of a 2 than a point guard.  Undersized for the 2 position.  Very streaky perimeter shooter.  Lacks great lateral quickness.

Gordon's ability to direct is key to his NBA future.
(Howie McCormick/Icon SMI)

Gordon has declared for the 2008 NBA draft, but hasn't hired an agent, preserving his college eligibility.
Late first to early second

Gordon knows how to score, but scouts feel he lacks the efficiency and polish to make a smooth transition to the NBA right now.  He's a likely second-round pick if he stays in the draft.  He'll likely return for his senior year at Mississippi State.

Slashing, athletic combo guard who has a very good feel for the game. Value goes up if he's a point guard given his size and toughness. Has a long wing span. Knows how to get to the rim.
Kyle Weaver's long arms have proven a great asset on defense.
(Christian Petersen/Getty Images)

High basketball IQ. Ultimate team player. Excellent, tenacious defender. His long arms and quickness allow him to really disrupt the passing lanes. Has improved his 3-point shooting tremendously this season.
His shooting is still suspect.  He doesn't have much of a midrange game and before this year he wasn't hitting 3s.  Doesn't seem to want to shoot the ball.  Averages only around eight shots a game.
Late first to early second

Offensively he's got a long way to go, but his basketball IQ is so high and his defense so good, more than one scout has projected him as a potential Bruce Bowen-type player in the pros.  He's a bubble first rounder at this point.

Larry Brown always wants a guy who will "play the right way," and that's Weaver. He's very talented, but totally unselfish. He is a great defender who also gets to the basket. If he ever develops a jump shot, he could be a very good pick here.
Unselfish, talented player.

picks.tradeNote: from GS via CHA, NYK, OKC and ATL

analysis.text: Big, athletic center with long arms.  Already has an NBA body.  Strong.  Wide shoulders. Soft hands.  Strong.  Quick on his feet.  Very mobile for a big guy.  Does most of his damage inside, but also has a solid jump shot.
Lacks experience.  Needs to get in much better shape.  His motor is inconsistent.  Still relatively unknown by NBA scouts.

Jawai is showing an impressive game Down Under.
(Photo by Lucas Dawson/Getty Images)

Plays for the Cairns Taipans in the Australian league as a rookie.
Mid to late first round

After watching him in a workout in Las Vegas -- he looks like a legit prospect. His size and strength make him a dominant force in Australia, and it looks like it can translate to the pros.  He looks like a poor man's Elton Brand.  He's a likely mid to late first round pick.

The Pacers are selecting Jawai for the Raptors. The Raptors got big with Jermaine O'Neal and they just got bigger with Jawai -- a huge player from Australia who looks like a bigger version of Elton Brand. Even though he's wide, he's pretty quick on his feet. He was a player in Australia, but it's a big leap to the NBA.
A wide body and quick on his feet.

Hendrix hopes his success can translate to the NBA.
(Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images)

A man child. NBA body and huge catcher's mitts for hands. Physical
player who works hard on the boards. Long arms allow him to play taller than he is. Good athlete. Developing a nice midrange game.
Lacks great foot speed.  Undersized for his college position for center.
Late first to early second

Hendrix had an excellent junior season at Alabama, but NBA scouts have been skeptical in the past.  They think Hendrix succeeds because of his strength.  Once he gets to the NBA, he'll look much more average.  Still, given the numbers he's put up at Alabama, you have to give him a look.

Hendrix really slipped for a guy who was so productive in the SEC. He's got huge hands, an NBA body and some rebounding skills. He's a bit undersized, but he has enough talent to make the league. At this point, another solid pick.
A bit undersized, but has huge hands.

Big-time athletic big man who plays with a lot of power in the paint.  Good rebounder and shot-blocker.  Gets most of his points off power dunks.  Excellent body and strength.  Plays with aggression.  Has good footwork.

Still very raw offensively.  Doesn't get involved in the offense at Cal.  Most of his shots are dunks. Poor free-throw shooter.  Zero ballhandling skills or perimeter game. Had shoulder surgery this summer.  Poor hands.

There's always room in the NBA for athletic big men like Hardin.
(Lisa Blumenfeld/Getty Images)

Hardin declared for the 2007 NBA draft on April 9, but withdrew after failing
to get a first-round promise. Suffered a stress fracture in his left foot in December, ending his season.
Late first to early second

Hardin was great in draft workouts last year and got considerable buzz as a potential lottery pick.  However, his senior season has been very disappointing.  He has the physical tools to be a Top 10 pick, but his play on the court suggests the second round.  Right now he's on the first-round bubble.
Erick Dampier

When you watch Hardin, you're wowed by his NBA body and athleticism. But does he really know how to play? Offensively he doesn't have much, but he should be able to play and defend in the league. Though I'm not sure the Sonics needed another big man prospect.
Not much offensively, but can defend.
Dorsey is an incredibly strong low-post player with explosive athleticism.  Can be a beast on the boards.  Good offensive rebounder.   Good shot-blocker.  Physical defender.
He's not much of an offensive threat.  He's a bit undersized to play his natural position at center.  He doesn't always play hard or committed.  Teams worry about his motor.

Dorsey's game reminds some of Ben Wallace's.
(San Antonio Express-News/ZUMA Press)
Late first to early second

Normally, players like Dorsey don't get a lot of love come draft time.  But the similarties to Ben Wallace's game will give them a second look.  He's not as good of a prospect as Big Ben because he doesn't have the same motor, but we expect to see him in a NBA uniform for a long time.
Ben Wallace

The Blazers have agreed to send the rights to Dorsey to the Rockets. Dorsey is a Ben Wallace clone -- a tough, physical rebounder and an explosive leaper and dunker. He's not a great offensive player and he can be inconsistent in his effort, but Dorsey is a good value pick here. The Rockets needed more toughness.
Tough, physical, and an explosive leaper.

picks.tradeNote: from CHA via SA, ATL and NYK

analysis.text: Athletic big man. Is an explosive jumper and plays aggressively.  Lefty. Long arms make him bigger than he's listed. Good scorer around the basket.  Quick for a big guy.  Runs the floor well.  Improving rebounder.
Needs to improve his shot-blocking. Needs to gain consistency.  He could play more physical.  Terrible free throw shooter.

Plaisted has potential to take his game beyond that of former Provo pivotmen Greg Kite and Shawn Bradley.
(AP Photo/Jae C. Hong)



Named the 2006 Mountain West Conference Freshman of the Year. Was a
medical redshirt his freshman season because of a knee injury.
Late first to early second.

After a stellar freshman season and a so-so sophomore campaign, he improved as a junior.  However scouts still wonder about his inconsistency. His combo of size and athleticism make him a legit first round prospect.  But his lack of production has raised plenty of red flags. Right now he's on the first round bubble.  He'll need strong workouts to get him in.

The Sonics are drafting for the Pistons. Plaisted is a nice player who was hurt by subpar measurements and a so-so Orlando pre-draft camp. But he's a great athlete who runs the floor, and he can do some things around the basket. There's good value here.
Can run the floor well. Good value here.

Draft profile coming soon ...
Josh Duncan helped push Xavier into the Elite Eight.
(AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill)
Second round to undrafted

picks.tradeNote: from PHI via HOU and OKC

analysis.text: Good athlete with some explosive leaping ability.  Runs the floor well.  Mostly a jump shooter with some nice range on this three point shot.  Can also put the ball on the floor and finish at the basket.
Lacks strength.  Poor rebounder for someone his size.  Inconsistent.   Doesn't dominate the way his skills suggest.  Has a knock of being a little passive on the court.
Plays for KK Split in the Adriatic League.   Averaged 10.5 ppg and 3.1 rpg in 25 mpg for Split in 2007-08
Second round to undrafted

Hairston is a power guard. He has great size, an NBA body and athleticism and a pretty advanced inside-outside game.

He's a jack-of-all-trades, master of none. He's not a great ballhandler. Some scouts question whether he has a real passion for the game.  It's not easy to tell.  Sometimes he just looks unselfish.  Other times he just disappears.  Injury prone.
Second round to undrafted

First, the good news. Hairston has great size, an NBA body and athleticism and a pretty advanced inside-outside game. However, Hairston hasn't taken his game to the next level the way scouts thought he could.  A strong NCAA Tournament performance the past two seasons helped his stock, but it's still unclear whether scouts will pull the trigger on him come draft night.

Hairston made 43.3 percent of 3-point shots in his senior year.
(Brian Spurlock/US Presswire)

A bigger version of Quentin Richardson.

Suns sent this pick to Spurs. Hairston doesn't do anything that wows you, but the guy really knows how to play. He can shoot the ball, has an NBA body and is very steady. I think he actually has enough talent to contribute a bit.
A steady swingman who can shoot the ball.

analysis.text:
Davon Jefferson is an intriguing prospect for many scouts.
Christian Petersen/Getty Images

Super athletic forward with explosive leaping ability and excellent quickness. Long arms and good strength allow him to be a force as an offensive rebounder. Good midrange shooter. Can create his shot off the dribble. Runs the floor very well. Plays well without the ball.
Needs to work on his ballhandling.  No deep range on his jump shot.  Basketball IQ is questioned by some scouts. Two years older than most NCAA freshmen.
Late first to early second

Jefferson is an intriguing prospect who is starting to live up to the hype he's had for the past several years.  His combination of size, athleticism and scoring ability make him a potential late first to early second-round pick.

Calathes has the game of a point guard in a 6-foot-10 body.  Very fluid athlete who can get up the floor.  Good ball handler for a big man.  Excellent court vision.  Good range on his jump shot. Versatile.
Good, but not great athlete.  Doesn't have great lateral quickness.   Who does he guard in the pros?  Needs to add strength.  Still finding his position.

Brother of Florida's Nick Calathes
Pat Calathes has grown in stature, along with his game.
(AP Photo/Al Behrman)
Second round to undrafted

Calathes used to be a point guard, but grew so rapidly it's taken a while for his game to fit into his body.  He was great in the Atlantic 10, but had a bomb in the opening round of the NCAA tournament.  A strong performance at Portsmouth helped him a little, but he's going to have to dominate at the Orlando camp to get solidly into the second round.

analysis.text: Excellent athlete with deep 3-point range. Big-time leaper. Long arms allow him to play bigger than he is. Quick release on his jumper plus great elevation on his jump shot make it hard to stop.  Has become an excellent rebounder for a guard.

No real midrange game to speak of, though he's done a better job at New Mexico of getting to the line.  Not a confident ball handler. Not a good defender, mostly from lack of effort, though his lateral quickness isn't great either.  Questionable attitude.  Not sure he has a real feel for the game.
Played two years at Kansas before transferring to New Mexico.  Sat out the 2005-06 season.  Was suspended from the New Mexico team in February of 2007 for "not being a good teammate."
Second round to undrafted

Has the talent to be a first-round pick ... but scouts are worried about work ethic and attitude. He's been a knucklehead for most of his career and most teams won't want to deal with the hassle for a second-round pick.

J.R. Smith
J.R. Giddens can play, but will he be a good fit for the NBA?
(AP Photo/Laura Rauch)

A huge surprise here. Giddens might have lottery-type talent, but he had so many off-court issues that his stock tanked. I guess Danny Ainge is willing to roll the dice, given his veteran squad. If Giddens grows up, this will be a great pick. But it's a big if ...
Off-court issues, but lottery type talent.

Quick, athletic point guard who thrives off penetration.  Long arms.  Fearless taking the ball to the basket.  Excellent passer who plays unselfishly. Good defender who can play with aggression. Good size for his position
Turnovers and shooting.  Dragic had almost as many turnovers as assists this season.  While his midrange game is fine, he's a marginal 3-point shooter.

Second round to undrafted.

Was a hot name in the spring of 2006, but the buzz lessened a bit since then.  His strong play in the European Championships last year in front of a host of scouts put him back on the radar screen.  With strong workouts he could be a solid second-round pick.

Spurs swapped this pick with the Suns. Dragic is a very athletic point guard who is excellent slashing to the basket. He doesn't have a great jump shot, but he's put up solid numbers in Europe. He's a nice player to stash in Europe for a few years.
An athletic point guard. Lacks a jumper.

Semih Erden could eventually develop into an NBA player.

Second round to undrafted

Erden has talent and has been on the international scouts radar for years.  He's slowly progressing as a player, but right now it's fair to say he's a project.  A team might be willing to draft him in the second round and keep him overseas for the next few years and see if he develops.
Erden is big, pretty athletic and fairly skilled. He can be a little wild on and off the court. Erden will be in Turkey for a while before he ever sees the NBA.
Will play in Europe long before the NBA.

He's big, strong (for a big guy) and plays with a lot of energy.  Nice, chiseled NBA body. Good mobility for someone his size. While you wouldn't call him athletic, he runs the floor well and is a pretty explosive leaper around the basket.  Likes to dunk on people. He's an aggressive rebounder and also has some decent low-post moves around the basket.
He's still pretty raw.  Didn't develop into a dominant force at Kansas as scouts thought he might.

Played high school ball in Melbourne, Fla., for the Florida Air Academy.
Sasha Kaun has impressed and disappointed scouts over the years.
(Orlin Wagner/AP Photo)
Second round to undrafted

Scouts were very impressed with Kaun at the Maui Invitational in 2005.  But he really regressed since then, in part, because of injuries.  He once was considered a potential late first round prospect, but he's no longer a lock for the second round.
Kaun has enough talent to be a backup big in the league, but he just agreed to a big contract in Russia. I'm not sure he'll ever be good enough to make more money in the NBA than he can in Russia.
Has talent, but will play in Russia.
